title: Committee of Supply – Head W (Ministry of Transport)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head W (Ministry of Transport)

sections.label: COVID-19 supply chain lessons
sections.summary: He moves to reduce Head W by $100 and says it is timely to take stock of COVID-19 supply chain disruption lessons and business responses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, I beg to move, "That the total sum to be allocated for Head W of the Estimates be reduced by $100." As we hopefully look to emerge from the COVID-19 pandemic year, it is timely for us to take stock of the lessons we have learnt from the supply chain disruptions amidst the COVID-19 pandemic and how businesses are responding to the same.

sections.label: Supply Chain 4.0 Initiative
sections.summary: He welcomes the Supply Chain 4.0 Initiative for small businesses but says Singapore must think about staying ahead as the transport node of choice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: But other larger and resource-rich countries will also see the same need now – whether it is using AI and machine learning to decrease dependency on human labour in critical parts of the supply chain or digitising the cumbersome paperwork that accompanies the cargo flowing through the chain.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: So, while I welcome the launch of our Supply Chain 4.0 Initiative to help small businesses scale up on digital and automated solutions to make supply chains more resilient and secure, we need to think about how we can continue to stay ahead as the transport node of choice.

sections.label: Idle state land use
sections.summary: He suggests the Government consider using idle state land, as part of the plan to move the sea port westwards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Perhaps the Government can consider how we can use idle state land to support this – as part of our more general plan to move our sea port westwards in the coming years.

sections.label: Smart Mobility 2030 masterplan
sections.summary: He asks how the Ministry will enhance Singapore as a reliable and resilient transport node, citing the Smart Mobility 2030 masterplan launched in 2014.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: How does the Ministry intend to further enhance Singapore as a reliable and resilient transport node?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: Under our Smart Mobility 2030 masterplan launched in 2014, we aim to optimise transport systems and enhance commuter travel experience across Singapore with the latest developments in transport technologies.

sections.label: Centralised information platform
sections.summary: He asks whether information can be centralised on a single user-friendly platform, noting a global chip shortage delayed Next-Gen-ERP rollout to the latter half of 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: Is there an opportunity to centralise information on a single user-friendly platform, now that a global chip shortage has delayed the rollout of the Next-Gen-ERP to the latter half of 2023?

sections.label: Decarbonising transport emissions
sections.summary: International climate change objectives have intensified the race to decarbonise transport, which accounts for around one-fifth of global carbon emissions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: International climate change objectives have intensified the race to decarbonise transport, which accounts for around one-fifth of global carbon emissions.

sections.label: Seaport results, air transport jobs
sections.summary: The seaport posted stellar results during the pandemic, but air transport and supporting services lost thousands of jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: While our seaport continued to post stellar results despite the pandemic, the same cannot be said about our air transport and supporting services industry, which has bled thousands of jobs since the pandemic broke.

sections.label: Air transport workforce drop
sections.summary: MOM data shows the air transport workforce dropped by about 30% compared to pre-COVID-19 staffing levels.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: According to MOM's data, our air transport workforce has dropped by about 30%, compared to pre-COVID-19 staffing levels.

sections.label: Low public transport ridership
sections.summary: LTA data shows 2021 public transport ridership averaged 5.25 million daily bus and train trips, the second lowest since 2010.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: According to data from LTA, public transport ridership in 2021 has continued to remain low.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: There was an average of 5.25 million bus and train trips a day, the second lowest since 2010 and much lower than the record 7.69 million daily trips in 2019.

sections.label: Singapore busiest transhipment port
sections.summary: MPA says Singapore was the world's busiest container transhipment port in 2021, handling a record 37.5 million TEUs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: According to MPA, Singapore was the world's busiest container transhipment port, handling a record high of 37.5 million twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs) of container throughput in 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: We are currently building the Tuas Mega Port which, when fully completed in 2040, will be the world's largest fully-automated terminal with the ability to handle up to 65 million TEUs annually.

sections.label: Post-pandemic work-from-home consensus
sections.summary: Business leaders consensus is that most staff, except frontline staff, will likely work from home 10% to 30% of the time post-pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: From my conversations with many business leaders, the consensus is that most staff, barring the frontline staff, will likely be working from home between 10% and 30% of the time even after the pandemic.

sections.label: Public Service work-from-home suggestion
sections.summary: A suggestion that the Public Service, employing about 130,000 officers, encourage staff to work from home one to two days a week.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Going forward, firstly, I would like to suggest that the Public Service, which employs about 130,000 public officers, consider encouraging their staff to continue to work from home one to two days a week or to allow the staff to come to work after morning peak hours.

sections.label: Free pre-peak MRT travel
sections.summary: In 2013 to 2014, commuters were offered free pre-peak travel if they exited certain MRT stations before 7.45 am.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: In 2013 to 2014, many of you would remember that commuters were offered free pre-peak travel if they exited certain MRT stations before 7.45 am.

sections.label: Expanding Singapore cycling path network
sections.summary: Singapore is expanding its 440-kilometre cycling path network to 800 kilometres by 2023 and 1,320 kilometres by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: As what Minister S Iswaran had said, commuting by bicycle does not emit any carbon dioxide.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: So, it is good that Singapore is expanding its current 440-kilometre network of cycling paths to 800 kilometres by 2023 and to 1,320 kilometres by 2030.

sections.label: AV and air taxi trials
sections.summary: MOT was asked for updates on AV trials at Jurong Innovation District, Tengah and Punggol, and on air taxi regulation and safety standards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Can MOT update on the progress of AV trials at Jurong Innovation District, Tengah and Punggol?

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Meanwhile, two air taxi pioneers had recently announced their ambition to launch commercial air taxi services in Singapore by 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Could MOT provide us an update on the regulatory framework and safety standard for air taxis in Singapore?

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Alongside pandemic-induced changes in the way we travel, new transport technologies like AVs and air taxis would be an important part of our transport strategy for the future to reduce traffic congestion and free up land for other uses.

sections.label: Russia oil supply disruptions
sections.summary: Russia accounts for about 10% of world crude oil supply, so sanctions will disrupt supplies and raise oil, jet fuel and plane ticket prices.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: As Russia accounts for about 10% of the world's supply of crude oil, there will be serious disruptions due to the sanctions against Russia by the international community.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: Not only will oil prices jump, there will also be an impact on the supplies of jet fuel and, in turn, an upward pressure on the price of plane tickets.

sections.label: Aviation sector manpower
sections.summary: The aviation sector is manpower-intensive, with more than 50,000 workers at Changi Airport pre-COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, the aviation sector is a manpower-intensive one, with more than 50,000 workers working in Changi Airport pre-COVID-19.

sections.label: Sustainable Air Hub advisory panel
sections.summary: The Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore convened the inaugural International Advisory Panel on Sustainable Air Hub meeting to develop a blueprint.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: Last month, the Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore convened the inaugural meeting of the International Advisory Panel on Sustainable Air Hub to develop a blueprint for Singapore to become a sustainable aviation hub.

sections.label: Asia Pacific travel decline
sections.summary: IATA figures show Asia Pacific travel in October 2021 was down 92.8% compared to October 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: According to figures released by the International Air Transport Association (IATA) for October last year, travel in the Asia Pacific was down 92.8% in October 2021, compared to October 2019.

sections.label: Singapore top bunkering port
sections.summary: MPA reported Singapore was top bunkering port in 2021 with 50.04 million tonnes total sales, mostly conventional.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: MPA has recently reported that in 2021, Singapore has kept its position as the top bunkering port, registering total bunker sales volume of 50.04 million tonnes in 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Of this, the bulk of the sales volume, 49.99 million tonnes to be exact, were conventional bunker sales, while only 0.5 million tonnes were in LNG bunker sales.

sections.label: Thomson-East Coast Line timeline
sections.summary: The question asks the Minister whether the Thomson-East Coast Line is on track to be fully operational by 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Thirdly, may I ask the Minister whether the construction of the Thomson-East Coast Line is on track to be fully operational by 2024?

sections.label: Public transport satisfaction survey
sections.summary: PTC survey found public transport satisfaction at a six-year low, with bus waiting times a factor, and calls for consultations before bus service changes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Public Transport Council (PTC)'s latest customer satisfaction survey found that satisfaction with public transport services has fallen to its lowest level in six years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The survey showed that discontent with public bus services was a factor with many commuters, notably expressing dissatisfaction with bus waiting times.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: These sentiments are similarly expressed by many of my residents living along Bedok Reservoir Road where four bus services were recently cut or re-routed last December.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Before removing or re-routing bus services, LTA should conduct public consultations with affected residents.

sections.label: Feeder bus waiting times
sections.summary: Commuters should not wait more than five minutes during peak hours or 10 minutes off-peak for feeder buses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Commuters should not have to wait more than five minutes during peak hours or 10 minutes during off-peak hours for feeder buses.

sections.label: Free transport concession card proposal
sections.summary: A proposal is shared for seniors and people with disabilities to receive a concession card for free public transport.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Chairman, I wish to share with this House a proposal that seniors and those with disabilities be furnished with a concession card that will allow them to ride public transportation free of charge.

sections.label: Free transport cost estimates
sections.summary: Conservative estimates put added expenditures at $0.3 billion to $0.4 billion a year, a 3% to 4% budget increase, with off-peak free transport suggested.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Our estimates, which are, admittedly, conservative, suggest added expenditures of between $0.3 billion and $0.4 billion a year, or an increase of 3% to 4% of the Ministry's current budget.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Even if we are uncomfortable with completely unrestricted free usage, one reasonable accommodation would be to allow such free transport during off-peak hours, where there is, typically, some spare capacity in our bus and train systems in any case.

sections.label: Free transport for seniors disabled
sections.summary: The speaker says society should at least give seniors and disabled free transport for dignity.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Even if we do not wish to push the argument that far, I believe we can all agree that the least an inclusive and caring society can do for our seniors and disabled is to afford them the dignity to move around our beautiful city, free of charge.

sections.label: Zero growth cars motorcycles
sections.summary: The Government announced a zero-growth rate for cars and motorcycles until 31 January 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Last year, the Government announced a zero-growth rate for cars and motorcycles until 31 January 2025.

sections.label: Category C goods vehicle growth
sections.summary: Goods vehicles are in Category C, allowed a growth rate of 0.25% of vehicle population divided by four until 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: For example, I note from the categorisation of vehicles for COE purposes, goods vehicles are in a separate category, Category C.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I further note that this category is allowed a growth rate of 0.25% of the vehicle population divided by four until 2025.

sections.label: New small motorcycle cost
sections.summary: A new small motorcycle with the same small engine capacity costs between $15,000 and $18,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: My recent engagement shows that owning a new small motorcycle with the same small engine capacity will cost between $15,000 and $18,000 dollars.

sections.label: Motorcycle premiums versus price
sections.summary: Premiums can now cost more than two times the price of an entry level motorcycle.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The premiums now can cost more than two times the price of an entry level motorcycle.

sections.label: Motorcycle COE prices and supply
sections.summary: MOT stopped the transfer to Open Category, moderating motorcycle COE prices, and is asked if more can be done and COE numbers increased.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: MOT has responded then by stopping the transfer to Open Category, which was helpful to moderate motorcycle COE prices then.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: In view of the current prices of motorcycle COEs, is there more that MOT can do and possibly increase the number of COEs for motorcycles?

sections.label: Enforcement against cyclists and PMD users
sections.summary: The Government is asked for a report of its past year's enforcement and engagements, including infringement cases by cyclists or PMD users.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Will the Government give a brief report of its enforcement and engagements over the past year, including the number of cases of infringements by cyclists or PMD users, who were taken to task?

sections.label: Active Mobility Advisory Panel recommendations
sections.summary: AMAP's recommendations came at a timely juncture to ensure safety as motorists and cyclists share roads, recommending cyclists take up third-party liability insurance.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Therefore, the recommendations from the Active Mobility Advisory Panel (AMAP) came at a timely juncture to ensure safety as motorists and cyclists increasingly share the roads.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am glad the Panel has recommended that cyclists take up third-party liability insurance.

sections.label: Catching errant cyclists and motorists
sections.summary: The Ministry is asked how errant cyclists and motorists will be caught and censured, with lanes proposed by Town Councils with LTA and piloted on less used roads.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: How will the Ministry be ensuring that errant cyclists and motorists will be caught and censured?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: These lanes would be proposed by the Town Councils in collaboration with LTA and can be piloted on roads that are less heavily utilised within their estates.

sections.label: Lanes supplementing bike trails
sections.summary: Lanes connecting within estates will supplement the tripling of bike trails envisioned in the Singapore Green Plan 2030.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Lanes that connect within estates will serve as an important supplement to the tripling of bike trails envisioned in the Singapore Green Plan 2030.

sections.label: Signs on path dangers
sections.summary: LTA is asked whether it can put up more prominent signs along paths reminding cyclists of the dangers of speeding and reckless riding.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Can LTA put up more prominent signs along the paths reminding cyclists on the dangers of speeding and riding recklessly?

sections.label: Islandwide cycling network safety update
sections.summary: The Ministry is asked for an update on the islandwide cycling network and plans to make cycling safer on pathways outside the network.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Can the Ministry share an update on the islandwide cycling network as well as plans to make cycling safer for cyclists and pedestrians on pathways which are currently not part of the network?

sections.label: WSG training allowance adjustment
sections.summary: WSG's training allowance is $4.50 per hour, and the Ministry is asked whether it will adjust training allowances.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: To provide some ground reality, the current training allowance provided by WSG is pegged at $4.50 per hour.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: An eight-hour training day equates to $36 or 50% of vehicle rental cost.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: As our drivers seek for more sustainable future-proof livelihoods, will the Ministry consider training allowances to be adjusted?

sections.label: New safety nets for drivers
sections.summary: The Government is asked what new safety nets it will put in place for drivers and how effective they have been since July 2021.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: What are some of the new safety nets that the Government will be putting in place to ensure that our drivers remain safe and how has it been effective as a deterrent for taxi drivers and PH drivers since its inclusion in July 2021?

sections.label: VTLs with 32 countries
sections.summary: VTLs with 32 countries and regions enabled passenger volumes of about 15% of pre-COVID-19 levels in December 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Today, we have VTLs with 32 countries and regions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: These VTLs have enabled us to attain passenger volumes of about 15% of pre-COVID-19 levels in December 2021.

sections.label: Changi passenger volume recovery targets
sections.summary: IATA forecasts Asia Pacific international passenger volumes recovering to about 40% of pre-COVID-19 levels this year, and Changi aims for at least 50% in 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: IATA forecasts that international passenger volumes in the Asia Pacific will recover to about 40% of pre-COVID-19 levels this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: We aim to restore Changi's passenger volumes to be at least 50% of pre-COVID-19 levels in 2022.

sections.label: OneAviation Resilience Package funding
sections.summary: The Government will support aviation with a $500 million OneAviation Resilience Package, allocating funds to manpower, cost relief, public health and digitalisation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: The Government will continue supporting our aviation sector amidst the continued uncertainty with a $500 million "OneAviation Resilience Package" in the coming financial year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Of this, $60 million will go towards manpower support, as companies build up capacity ahead of demand; $390 million for continued cost relief and measures to safeguard public health at the airport; and $50 million to support long-term industry digitalisation and transformation efforts via a top-up to the Aviation Development Fund.

sections.label: Port terminal emissions reduction
sections.summary: Terminal operators will electrify equipment, optimise energy and use renewables, targeting at least 60% emissions cut from 2005 levels by 2030 and net-zero by 2050.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Our terminal operators will electrify equipment, optimise energy usage and leverage renewable energy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: We aim to reduce emissions by at least 60% from 2005 levels by 2030 and achieve net-zero emissions at our port terminals by 2050.

sections.label: MPA green funding commitment
sections.summary: MPA will commit an additional $300 million over 10 years to cut port terminal and harbour craft emissions and support green technologies and fuels.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Third, MPA will commit an additional $300 million in funding over the next 10 years to reduce emissions from our port terminals and harbour craft and support the development of green technologies and fuels for international shipping.

sections.label: Peak hour active journey share
sections.summary: The proportion of peak hour walk, cycle or ride journeys completed within 45 minutes rose from 66% in 2019 to 71% in 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: The proportion of peak hour walk, cycle or ride journeys completed within 45 minutes has increased from 66% in 2019 to 71% in 2021.

sections.label: Rail network expansion
sections.summary: When these lines are completed, the rail network would have increased by 50% to 360 kilometres.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: When these lines are completed, we would have increased our rail network by 50% to 360 kilometres.

sections.label: Early MRT tap-in discount
sections.summary: Commuters tapping in at any MRT or LRT station before 7.45 am on weekdays, excluding public holidays, enjoy a discount of up to 50 cents.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Today, commuters who tap-in at any MRT or LRT station before 7.45 am on weekdays, excluding public holidays, enjoy a discount of up to 50 cents.

sections.label: Public Transport Vouchers funding
sections.summary: In the last two Fare Review Exercises, approximately $20 million a year was set aside in Public Transport Vouchers to defray the fare increase impact.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: In addition, in the last two Fare Review Exercises, for example, we set aside approximately $20 million a year in Public Transport Vouchers to help defray the impact of the fare increase.

sections.label: Public transport commuter subsidies
sections.summary: The Government spends over $2 billion annually on public transport subsidies, about $1 billion each for bus and train operations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Overall, the Government spends more than $2 billion annually in subsidies for public transport commuters: about $1 billion for bus operations and $1 billion for train operations.

sections.label: Fare increase burden and seniors
sections.summary: Adult fares would rise 20% to 25%, or 30 to 40 cents, and the burden grows by 2030 as seniors and persons with disabilities increase.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: If borne by commuters, adult fares will have to be increased by around 20% to 25% today, or 30 cents to 40 cents on average – this is up to 11 times the fare increase last year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: This financial burden is by no means insignificant and it will only grow by 2030, when the number of persons with disabilities and seniors aged 60 and above is expected to increase, by about 28%, to about 1.2 million.

sections.label: Motorcycle TCOE demand
sections.summary: Demand for motorcycles is strong, with motorcycle TCOE utilisation rates consistently above 99% since bidding resumed in July 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: However, it is important to note that there has been strong and persistent demand for motorcycles.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: This is reflected in the utilisation rate of motorcycle Temporary Certificates of Entitlement, or TCOEs, which have remained consistently high at over 99% since bidding resumed in July 2020.

sections.label: Motorcycle COE distribution and review
sections.summary: Most COEs went to motorcycles of 200 cc or less, but limited COE supply risks price volatility; LTA is reviewing this.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: The distribution of these COEs is also noteworthy: 70% have been used for motorcycles with 200 cc engine capacity or less, about 20% in the 201 cc to 400 cc range and about 10% are more than 400 cc.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: But the problem is that the overall number of COEs available is between 400 and 600, on average, per bidding cycle exercise.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: That being the case, if we further subdivide the category, the likelihood of greater volatility in the prices is significantly increased.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Having said that, we have observed early signs that the utilisation rate may be softening for TCOEs obtained in more recent months.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: So, I want to assure Members that I have asked LTA to study this very carefully and they will be completing their review soon.

sections.label: Shortened bus services
sections.summary: Three bus services were shortened on 12 December 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: On Mr Gerald Giam's questions, we shortened three bus services on 12 December 2021.

sections.label: Pre-COVID ridership drop
sections.summary: Before COVID-19, ridership for the three services dropped 32% to 55% on parts of the routes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: If we look at the data before COVID-19, the sustained drop in ridership for these three services ranged from 32% to 55% for parts of the routes.

sections.label: Bus service subsidy savings
sections.summary: Shortening three bus services saved $9.5 million in yearly subsidies, which can be reallocated to new bus services.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: The shortening of the three bus services, for example, saved $9.5 million of subsidies per year, which can be reallocated to new bus services.

sections.label: Container throughput and IMC
sections.summary: Container throughput hit a new high of 37.5 million TEUs, and the IMC attracted 23 companies to expand or set up in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Container throughput reached a new high of 37.5 million twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs), while our IMC attracted 23 companies to expand or set up operations in Singapore.

sections.label: Tuas Port capacity
sections.summary: When completed, Tuas Port can handle up to 65 million TEUs a year, 50% more than current capacity.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: When completed, Tuas Port can handle up to 65 million TEUs a year, 50% more than our current capacity.

sections.label: Sea Transport jobs target
sections.summary: The Sea Transport sector aims to create 1,000 good local jobs from 2020 to 2025, including maritime and emerging roles.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: In response to Mr Saktiandi and Mr Melvin Yong, the Sea Transport sector aims to create 1,000 good jobs for locals between 2020 and 2025, including traditional maritime jobs like seafarers and port operation managers, and many emerging roles such as software engineers and supply chain managers.

sections.label: SailMAP seafarer funding
sections.summary: MPA and tripartite partners will provide an additional $12.5 million for SailMAP, plus an accelerated marine engineer training pathway.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Beyond the existing scholarships, MPA and our tripartite partners will provide an additional $12.5 million to fund a new Sail Milestone Achievement Programme (SailMAP) to enhance the retention of local seafarers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Over the next five years, up to 250 local seafarers can receive up to $50,000 each, when they attain key career milestones.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Most of the funding will come from the Government and the remainder will be funded by the Singapore Shipping Association, SMOU and SOS as part of this tripartite partnership.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: In addition, we will launch an accelerated training pathway for individuals with mechanical engineering backgrounds to become shipboard marine engineers, shortening the duration from the current 120 weeks to 22 weeks.

sections.label: Sea Transport career conversions
sections.summary: Since 2018, about 200 mid-career workers converted skills through Sea Transport Career Conversion Programmes, including 30 PMETs placed in 14 companies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Since 2018, we have helped around 200 mid-career workers undergo skills conversion to take up new roles through Career Conversion Programmes (CCP) in the Sea Transport sector.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: This includes 30 PMETs who have been successfully placed in new roles in 14 companies under the enhanced CCP for Sea Transport Professionals and Associates launched in November last year.

sections.label: Driver relief fund support
sections.summary: Close to 50,000 drivers received over $390 million from the Special Relief Fund and COVID-19 Driver Relief Fund, with trips at about 75% of pre-COVID-19 levels.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Close to 50,000 drivers benefited from over $390 million of support through the Special Relief Fund and COVID-19 Driver Relief Fund.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: The number of trips is about 75% of pre-COVID-19 levels, up from about 25% during the circuit breaker period.

sections.label: Electric taxi fleet target
sections.summary: At least half of the taxi fleet will be electric by 2030, up from about 2% today.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: At least half of our taxi fleet will be electric by 2030, up from about 2% today.

sections.label: Bus, cycling, walking corridors
sections.summary: Another 60 kilometres of corridors with bus, cycling lanes and footpaths will be added by 2030, including the longest TPC along the North South Corridor.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: These corridors incorporate bus, cycling lanes and footpaths for all.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: We will add another 60 kilometres of these corridors by 2030, including the longest TPC along the North South Corridor.

sections.label: Civic District and Tiong Bahru footpaths
sections.summary: Pedestrians can walk freely past landmarks like the Padang and Esplanade Park, and roadside car parks along Seng Poh Road will become wider footpaths.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Pedestrians can now walk freely and enjoy the picturesque landscape, as they visit key landmarks, such as the Padang and the Esplanade Park or various art and cultural institutes, all without having to worry about traffic and fumes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: This has also opened up opportunities for us to work with stakeholders in the Civic District to bring new arts and cultural activities outdoors to further enliven the area.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Residents in Tiong Bahru, a popular neighbourhood, can look forward to wider footpaths and more community spaces.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: We will convert the roadside car parks along Seng Poh Road to wider footpaths.

sections.label: Silver Zones in towns
sections.summary: LTA will implement another 28 Silver Zones by 2025 in towns such as Tampines, Ang Mo Kio and West Coast.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: LTA will implement another 28 Silver Zones by 2025 in towns, such as Tampines, Ang Mo Kio and West Coast.

sections.label: Speed limiter regime for lorries
sections.summary: The Traffic Police will expand the speed limiter regime to cover all lorries of MLW above 3.5 tonnes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: The Traffic Police (TP) will be expanding the speed limiter regime to encompass all lorries of MLW above 3.5 tonnes.

sections.label: Driver rest and lorry in-charge
sections.summary: MOM will require employers to give drivers sufficient rest and mandate a vehicle person-in-charge on lorries ferrying workers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: MOM will introduce new measures to require employers to provide sufficient rest for their drivers, in particular, those who play dual roles of a driver and ground worker.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: MOM will also mandate that every lorry ferrying workers have a designated vehicle person-in-charge who will sit next to the driver.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: This person-in-charge will be empowered to stop the driver from driving if he deems the driver to be unfit for driving.

sections.label: Lorry covers mandate
sections.summary: LTA, supported by MOM, will mandate covers on all lorries used to ferry workers, with details shared later.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: LTA, with the support of MOM, have decided to mandate the installation of such covers on all lorries used to ferry workers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: We will share implementation details at a later date.

sections.label: Improving land transport system
sections.summary: The land transport system will be improved through new technologies, worker upskilling and refreshed infrastructure design, with safety foremost.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Chairman, in conclusion, we will improve our land transport system by adopting new technologies, upskilling our workers and refreshing our approach to infrastructure design, all while maintaining safety at the forefront.

sections.label: Cycling network expansion
sections.summary: The cycling network will grow from around 500 kilometres today to 800 kilometres in two to three years and about 1,300 kilometres by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: The cycling network is around 500 kilometres long today.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: We will grow it to 800 kilometres in the next two to three years and eventually reach our target of around 1,300 kilometres in year 2030.

sections.label: Off-road accidents and rider tests
sections.summary: Off-road accidents involving active mobility devices have fallen 40% since 2019, and close to 31,000 riders have passed the tests.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Notably, the number of off-road accidents involving active mobility devices has decreased by 40% since 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: To date, close to 31,000 riders have passed the tests.

sections.label: Visual communication tool for commuters
sections.summary: With the Singapore Association for the Deaf, a visual communication tool will be introduced in all MRT stations and bus interchanges by end 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: First, to better support communication between commuters and public transport staff, we are working with the Singapore Association for the Deaf to introduce a visual communication tool in all MRT stations and bus interchanges by end 2022.

sections.label: Dementia Go-To-Points transport nodes
sections.summary: Public transport nodes are to be listed as Dementia Go-To-Points by end 2022, working with operators.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: With an ageing population, conditions such as dementia will likely be more prevalent.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Hence, we are working with public transport operators to list all public transport nodes as Dementia Go-To-Points by end 2022.

sections.label: Stroller restraints on public buses
sections.summary: Stroller restraints are installed on all public buses, making travel more convenient for families with young children.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: In addition, families travelling with young children in strollers will find it more convenient now that stroller restraints are installed on all public buses.

sections.label: Volunteer sign-ups since launch
sections.summary: More than 500 people have signed up as volunteers since its launch in December 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Since its launch in December 2020, more than 500 people have signed up as volunteers.

sections.label: Enhanced penalties for illegal modifications
sections.summary: Penalties and fines for illegal modifications were enhanced, a motorcyclist was fined $1,200, and courts may detain repeat offenders' motorcycles.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Since last year, in July, we have enhanced the penalty framework and doubled the fines for illegal modifications.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: On 1 March this year, a motorcyclist was fined $1,200 for illegal modification of his exhaust system.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: We have also decided to enhance the penalty framework by, for instance, applying to the Courts for second and subsequent offenders to have their motorcycles detained for up to three months for illegal modification.

sections.label: Questioning $300-400 million proposal
sections.summary: Raising questions about a proposal costing $300 million to $400 million more a year is not penny wise and pound foolish.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: When a proposal is made that will incur $300 million to $400 million more a year, when we raise questions about that, I do not think that is being penny wise and pound foolish.

sections.label: Peak bus loads after adjustments
sections.summary: After Mr Giam shared feedback with LTA, which worked with the operator, peak loads dropped from 70-75% to below 45%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Before Mr Giam shared the feedback with us, the maximum load during peak periods was about 70% to 75%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: When Mr Giam shared the feedback with LTA, LTA then worked with the operator to make some adjustments and the peak loads have now dropped to below 45%.

sections.label: Morning peak bus frequency
sections.summary: LTA asked the bus operator to increase frequency between 6 am and 6.45 am during the morning peak.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: During the morning peak, between 6 am and 6.45 am, LTA has asked the bus operator to increase the frequency, precisely because we understand that this is the peak period.

sections.label: Off-peak free ridership possibility
sections.summary: A question is raised about the possibility of free ridership during off-peak hours even if MOT finds unconstrained subsidy unaffordable.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Which is that even if MOT believes that an unconstrained subsidy is unaffordable, what of the possibility of free ridership during off-peak hours?

sections.label: Member's cost estimate
sections.summary: The Member's estimate is $300 million to $400 million, which the speaker does not agree with.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: By the Member’s estimate – I am not saying that I agree with his estimate – but his estimate is $300 million to $400 million.

sections.label: Ministry budget development expenditure
sections.summary: The Ministry's $11 billion budget includes two-thirds which is development expenditure.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: The Ministry’s budget of $11 billion includes two-thirds which is development expenditure.

sections.label: Subsidy increase proposal percentage
sections.summary: Discounting COVID-19 measures, the Member's proposal is a subsidy increase of about 20% to 25% using a $2 billion reference point.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Specifically, the Ministry’s operating budget in the last couple of years has been increased because of COVID-19-specific measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: So, if you discount that further, what the Member is actually proposing is an increase in the subsidies – if I use my $2 billion reference point – of about 20% to 25%.

sections.label: Workers' Party alternate levers
sections.summary: The Workers' Party has put up four alternate levers as part of this Budget debate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Indeed, as part of this Budget debate, the Workers' Party has put up four alternate levers.

sections.label: Budget balance and financial sustainability
sections.summary: The passage states that proposals must balance quality service, affordability and financial sustainability, and address costs within a Ministry's budget rather than at a macro level.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Every year, we have to address this issue of the balance between quality service, affordability and financial sustainability.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: So, when we make proposals, it cannot be that we make proposals that incur additional expenses under one Head, but then, say it will all be taken care of at some macro level.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Because we do need the discipline of also addressing how, within that particular Ministry’s budget, we are making every effort to find the appropriate balance.

sections.label: Air, land and sea efforts
sections.summary: The passage states that air, land and sea were discussed, and looks forward to efforts for air and sea hubs, jobs, cycling paths, TEL, JRL and CRL.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: And we have discussed today quite a significant range on air, land and sea.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I am really looking forward to all our efforts to make our air and sea hubs status thrive again: the job opportunities that Senior Minister of State Chee mentioned just now in maritime Singapore and in various other sectors, the dedicated cycling paths that are going to come on stream and also the TEL, JRL and CRL.
